standard.title: Interpret and translate texts
standard.description: interpret and translate a range of non-verbal, spoken and written texts, and explain how meaning is conveyed to reflect cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interpret and produce bilingual texts, manage register conversion, and handle culturally-embedded language (AC9LCH8EC04). They have interpreted for others in familiar contexts. They have not yet interpreted for high-stakes cross-cultural events, managed idiom and cultural term challenges at the extended text level, or produced subtitled multimodal translations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret and translate a range of texts — including idioms, culture-specific terms, and extended texts — explaining how meaning is conveyed to reflect cultural context, purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Comparing translations and culture-specific terms
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare different translations of the same text or expression, evaluate translation choices, and explain strategies for handling culture-specific terms.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare at least two translations of the same expression or short text, evaluate the difference, and explain the strategy used to handle at least one culture-specific term.
nodes.typical_width: Compare and discuss various target language translations of English words and expressions; identify words used with specific cultural assumptions — gender, formality, significance; consider strategies for translating culture-specific terms; use resources including online tools to understand emerging new words.
wider: Research the translation history of a specific culture-specific term — document different translation approaches across contexts and evaluate which works best for which audience
Compare how the same culture-specific concept is handled across multiple published bilingual texts — identify patterns in translation strategy and evaluate effectiveness
nodes.hinge_reason: Translation comparison and culture-specific term handling are the prerequisites for high-stakes interpretation. Students who cannot compare and evaluate translation choices cannot produce culturally accurate interpretations for complex or formal contexts.

response_modes.reason: Translation comparison requires systematic analysis — students need a framework for evaluating what is gained and lost in each translation choice. Explicit comparative analysis with documented reasoning builds the evaluative capacity needed.

success_criteria: Compares at least two translations of the same expression or text and evaluates the difference
Explains the strategy used to handle at least one culture-specific term

nodes.label: Interpreting for cross-cultural events
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret for Chinese and English speakers in contexts requiring in-depth cross-cultural knowledge, applying strategies to mediate embedded cultural values.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret at least one exchange in a context requiring cross-cultural knowledge, applying at least one strategy for mediating cultural values or embedded meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret for Chinese and English speakers at events requiring cross-cultural knowledge; compare idioms and colloquialisms across languages; identify challenges in mediating embedded cultural values; interpret meaning in bilingual contexts; identify potential issues in cultural mediation.
wider: Interpret in a complex cross-cultural scenario where embedded cultural values create mediation challenges — document the challenges and the strategies used
Compare own real-world interpreting experience with the structured approaches introduced in this descriptor — identify what is already intuitive and what requires explicit development

response_modes.reason: Cross-cultural interpreting requires practice across varied event types and cultural knowledge domains. Varied interpreting scenarios — formal events, community gatherings, media contexts — build the flexible cultural mediation capacity needed.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students who interpret in family and community contexts bring authentic interpreting experience. Width investment here formalises and extends this practice — building conscious cultural mediation strategies on top of existing intuitive capacity.
success_criteria: Interprets an exchange in a context requiring cross-cultural knowledge
Applies at least one strategy for mediating cultural values or embedded meaning

nodes.label: Extended text translation and multimodal bilingual production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can translate extended texts and produce multimodal bilingual resources — subtitled videos, captioned presentations, bilingual cultural products — that accurately convey meaning across both languages.
nodes.minimum_width: Translate a short extended text (at least 8 sentences) or produce a multimodal bilingual resource, demonstrating accurate meaning transfer and at least two deliberate translation decisions.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment with translations of extended texts using dictionaries, translation tools and own knowledge; compare bilingual editions of stories or poems; produce subtitles for Chinese or English programs; create multimodal bilingual products for cultural audiences; apply translation strategies in extended contexts.
wider: Produce a fully subtitled bilingual video — evaluate accuracy and cultural appropriateness with a target audience and revise

Compare own translation of an extended text with an existing published translation — identify every difference, evaluate the choices, and discuss what the comparison reveals about translation as cultural interpretation

response_modes.reason: Extended text translation integrates comparison and evaluation skills (node 1) and cross-cultural interpretation (node 2) into a full sustained translation act. The teaching investment is in creating real-audience conditions — actual subtitling, real community events — where translation accuracy has genuine communicative stakes.

success_criteria: Translates a short extended text or produces a multimodal bilingual resource with accurate meaning transfer
Demonstrates at least two deliberate translation decisions beyond word-for-word substitution
